question: A Cisco ACI engineer must configure an access port on a Cisco ACI leaf switch. The access policy should be configured so that it supports L3Out connectivity concurrently with several EPGs that are mapped to this interface with the static port method. How should the access policy be configured?
options: by linking the interface policy group to multiple Attachable Access Entity Profiles
with two interface policy groups that are linked to the same interface profile port selector
by mapping a single physical domain, mapped to the L3out and EPG interfaces
with a single Attachable Access Entity Profile that is linked to the corresponding routed domain and physical domain
theory: An Attachable Access Entity Profile (AEP) links physical leaf ports to one or more domains, and a single port can carry both routed (L3Out) and bridged (EPG) traffic concurrently only if that port's AEP is associated with both a routed domain (for the L3Out) and a physical domain (for the statically bound EPGs) at the same time. Splitting these across multiple AEPs or interface policy groups on the same port isn't how ACI resolves simultaneous L3Out and EPG traffic on one interface — the single AEP simply needs both domain associations. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI Attachable Entity Profiles)
